facts.fact_text: According to the applicant, the demonstrations of 31 July 2010 and 10 March 2013 were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicant, the demonstrations of 31 July 2010 and 10 March 2013 were conducted in a peaceful manner.
According to the applicant, the participants of the demonstration of 31 July 2010 were demanding free and fair elections and democratic reforms in Azerbaijan.
According to the applicant, the participants of the demonstration of 10 March 2013 were protesting over the deaths of numerous soldiers in the army.
A demonstration was planned to be held on 31 July 2010 in Baku.
A demonstration was planned to be held on 10 March 2013 in Baku.
On 23 July 2010 the organisers, consisting of several members of opposition parties, gave notice to the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) of the demonstration planned for 31 July 2010.
It appears that no prior notice was given to the Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) by the organisers of the demonstration of 10 March 2013.
The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) refused to authorise the demonstration of 31 July 2010 at the places indicated by the organisers.
The organisers decided to hold the demonstrations in the centre of Baku despite the Baku City Executive Authority's refusal to authorise the demonstration at the places indicated.
Shortly after the demonstration of 31 July 2010 had begun, the police started to disperse those who had gathered.
Shortly after the demonstration of 10 March 2013 had begun, the police started to disperse those who had gathered.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation at the demonstration of 31 July 2010.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation at the demonstration of 10 March 2013.
On the day of the applicant's arrest following the demonstration of 31 July 2010, an administrative offence report (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) was issued on the applicant.
On the day of the applicant's arrest following the demonstration of 10 March 2013, an administrative offence report (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) was issued on the applicant.
By a decision of 31 July 2010, the Sabail District Court (first-instance court) convicted the applicant under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
By a decision of 31 July 2010, the Sabail District Court (first-instance court) sentenced the applicant to seven days' administrative detention.
By a decision of 11 March 2013, the Sabail District Court (first-instance court) convicted the applicant under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
By a decision of 11 March 2013, the Sabail District Court (first-instance court) sentenced the applicant to seven days' administrative detention.
On 16 August 2010, the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal in the first case and upheld the decision of the Sabail District Court (first-instance court) of 31 July 2010.
On 27 March 2013, the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal in the second case and upheld the decision of the Sabail District Court (first-instance court) of 11 March 2013.

At the time of the applicant's arrests on 31 July 2010 and 10 March 2013, under Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, no prior written notification was required for spontaneous assemblies.

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 31 July 2010, Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 (CAO) provided that any breach of the rules, set forth under the legislation, on the organisation and holding of assemblies, demonstrations, protests, marches and pickets shall be punishable by a reprimand or a fine of seven to thirteen manats (AZN).

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 31 July 2010, Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 (CAO) provided that deliberate failure by an individual to comply with a lawful order of a police officer or military serviceman carrying out their duties to protect public order shall be punishable by a fine of twenty to twenty-five manats (AZN) or, if that sanction is inadequate in the circumstances of the case and taking into account the character of the offender, by up to fifteen days' administrative detention.

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 31 July 2010, Article 410.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 (CAO) provided that an individual who is subject to administrative offence proceedings or a representative of a legal entity shall be given an opportunity to familiarise himself with the administrative offence report.

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 31 July 2010, Article 410.4 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 (CAO) provided that an individual who is subject to administrative offence proceedings or a representative of a legal entity has the right to a copy of the administrative offence report.

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 31 July 2010, Article 437.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 (CAO) provided that a copy of a decision delivered on the basis of an appeal or a protest against a decision in an administrative offence case shall be given to the individual with respect to whom the decision in an administrative offence case was adopted within three days of its adoption.

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 31 July 2010, Article 437.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences 2000 (CAO) provided that a copy of a decision delivered on the basis of an appeal or a protest against a decision sentencing an individual to administrative detention shall be given to that individual on the day of its adoption.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 entered into force on 1 January 2013.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced new wording to Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) concerning breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies.

Following the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies became explicitly punishable under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced for the first time a punishment in the form of administrative detention of up to 15 days under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced community service as a new form of punishment under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 increased the fine for breaching the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies to between AZN 300 and 600 for participants of an assembly.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 increased the fine for breaching the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies to between AZN 1,500 and 3,000 for individuals who organise an assembly.

Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 increased the fine for breaching the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies to between AZN 3,000 and 6,000 for persons in charge (vəzifəli şəxslər) who organise an assembly.

Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 increased the fine for breaching the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies to between AZN 15,000 and 30,000 for legal entities involved in the organisation of an assembly.
By Law no. 457-IVQD of 2 November 2012, which entered into force on 29 November 2012, the fine set out in Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) was increased to AZN 200.
The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) refused to authorise the demonstration of 31 July 2010 at the places indicated by the organisers.

The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) proposed three alternative locations on the outskirts of Baku for the demonstration of 31 July 2010: a stadium situated in the Binagadi District, a square near Zigh Road in the Khatai District, and the yard of a driving school situated in the 20th habitable area of the Sabail District.
The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) noted that of the locations proposed by the organisers at which to hold the assembly, the squares were all designated public leisure areas.
The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) noted that of the locations proposed by the organisers at which to hold the assembly, the other places (apart from the squares) were areas with heavy traffic.

The administrative offence report issued following the applicant's arrest on 31 July 2010 stated that by deliberately failing to comply with a lawful order of the police, the applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).

Following the applicant's arrest on 10 March 2013, the applicant was charged with an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) (participation in a public assembly organised not in accordance with the law).

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe, titled 'The honouring of obligations and commitments by Azerbaijan', stated that there is no political dialogue with the opposition parties outside parliament in Azerbaijan.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that the Parliamentary Assembly is concerned by the restrictive climate for the activities of the extra-parliamentary opposition in Azerbaijan, which complains about limitations imposed on freedom of expression and freedom of assembly and the lack of access to the public media.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that the establishment of an inclusive political system and a truly competitive and unrestrictive political environment in Azerbaijan requires full implementation of basic freedoms, including freedom of expression, freedom of assembly and freedom of association.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that the situation in Azerbaijan regarding basic freedoms is preoccupying and the Parliamentary Assembly expressed its deep concern in this regard.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that recently adopted amendments to the Criminal Code and the Administrative Code of Azerbaijan, which increased penalties for the organisers of and participants in 'unauthorised' gatherings, raise concern.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that, considering the Azerbaijani authorities' ongoing blanket ban on protests in the Baku city centre, the amendments increasing penalties for organisers of and participants in 'unauthorised' gatherings are likely to have a further negative impact on freedom of assembly and freedom of expression.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that the restrictive use of certain articles of the Criminal Code of Azerbaijan, in particular Articles 221 and 233, against participants in peaceful, albeit unauthorised, demonstrations, is a matter of concern.
The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 was authored by Nils Muižnieks, the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, following his visit to Azerbaijan from 22 to 24 May 2013.

The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 by Nils Muižnieks, Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, stated that the Commissioner is deeply concerned by the recent amendments to the Law on Freedom of Assembly, the Criminal Code and the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan, which further erode the right to freedom of assembly.

The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 by Nils Muižnieks, Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, stated that the sanctions which can now be imposed, coupled with the fact that local authorities have not authorised a single rally in Baku city centre in recent years, clearly have a chilling effect on the organisation of or participation in demonstrations in Azerbaijan.

The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 by Nils Muižnieks, Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, stated that participants in peaceful assemblies should not be sanctioned for the mere fact of being present at and actively participating in the demonstration in question, provided they do not do anything illegal, violent or obscene in the course of it.

The Report (CommDH(2013)14) of 6 August 2013 by Nils Muižnieks, Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe, urged the Azerbaijani authorities to ensure that no disproportionate sanction, which would undermine the fundamental right to peaceful assembly, is imposed.
